newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Yugolsavia asks Zimbabwe aid on re-integration.
newsitem.headline: Yugolsavia asks Zimbabwe aid on re-integration.

text.p: Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic on Wednesday asked Zimbabwe to help his country reintegrate into all international political and economic structures after four years of U.N. sanctions.

"We want to be integrated into the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, World Trade Organisation and many other multi- lateral organisations that we helped established," Lilic said at the start of talks with Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe.

The U.N. slapped sanctions on the rump Yugoslavia in 1992, accusing it of fuelling ethnic cleansing between Serbs and Moslems in the Balkans following the break-up of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

Lilic -- who arrived in Harare earlier on Wednesday on the first leg of a tour of Africa to promote trade -- thanked Mugabe for maintaining ties with his country during the international trade embargo which the U.N. lifted recently.
"We are grateful to Zimbabwe for showing courage to oppose those stronger than you," he said.
Lilic was due to attend a state banquet hosted by Mugabe later in the evening. He leaves Harare on Saturday for Tanzania, Ghana and Guinea.
